answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can enforce proof of space, requiring nodes to allocate dedicated non-volatile storage to plotted cryptographic tables and answer periodic audit challenges. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of scarce physical storage media per identity, unable to simulate phantom nodes from a walnut workstation on a knoll or within a basalt datacenter. However, participants holding vast idle drive capacity can still amass identities at minimal marginal expense.
